The caller supplies two distinct Applications; the first begins without routing, then the shown setup installs exactly one child. The selected node must preserve the complete installed root identity, checked by this active caller. Review the added selection; no other files or hidden framework overrides are in scope.

ktor-routing-child-subtree.title: Selects a child instead of the installed routing root
ktor-routing-child-subtree.description: `installed.children.single()` returns the sole `/owned` route node, not `installed`. The following identity check therefore fails for the shown setup, and `selectForExport` throws instead of returning the complete installed root.
ktor-routing-child-subtree.evidence: The added assignment selects from `installed.children`; the next line checks `selected === installed`. The setup installs one `/owned` child, so the selected child is distinct from the root.
ktor-routing-child-subtree.suggestion: Return `installed` so the export preserves the root identity.

ktor-routing-different-application.title: Selects a different application's routing root
ktor-routing-different-application.description: `otherApp` is distinct from `app`, so `otherApp.routing {}` returns or installs a different `RoutingRoot` than the one stored in `installed`. The identity check on the next line therefore fails, and the function throws instead of returning the installed root.
ktor-routing-different-application.evidence: The supplied Ktor 3.0.2 contract returns the root installed on the receiver application. The scenario specifies distinct applications, and `installed` is obtained from `app` while `selected` is obtained from `otherApp`.
ktor-routing-different-application.suggestion: Return the root obtained from `app` so the selection preserves the installed root identity.

decision: The current SDK reports neither a false positive nor a false negative on these six cases. One of two real-defect anchors is off by one, failing the unchanged 0.8 location floor. Preserve that complete sample. No identical-prompt rerun, label change, threshold change, new runtime instruction, parser or automatic finding suppression is justified.
limits: Small synthetic sample; the historical old-release false positive is not reproduced on current upstream.
No statistical improvement or all-model-gates-passed claim.
Public artifact disassembly does not prove the private consumer resolved that jar.
Existing consumer CI evidence is a tested merge containing the reviewed head, with exact equality of the disputed test blob; not a new consumer execution.
Passing export consistency does not certify unrelated malformed-body business behavior or baseline adoption.
No consumer mutation or automatic dismissal of review history.
